svg.aria-label: Diagram: what setting the Amazon SNS MaximumMessageSize attribute above 256 KiB changes about a topic. On the left, a default SNS standard topic: message size is capped at 262,144 bytes, which is 256 KiB, but the topic can fan out to every delivery protocol SNS supports, including SQS, Lambda, Firehose, HTTP and HTTPS endpoints, email, SMS and mobile push, and the default subscriptions quota is 12,500,000 per topic. On the right, the same topic once MaximumMessageSize is raised above 256 KiB: payloads may reach 1 MiB, a fourfold increase, but the topic supports only Amazon SQS, Amazon Data Firehose and AWS Lambda subscriptions, and is capped at 100 total subscriptions. A panel in the middle records that this is a trade rather than an upgrade, since the same attribute that quadruples the payload reduces the subscription ceiling sharply and removes every human-facing delivery protocol. A panel at the bottom records that the older path still exists and still goes further: the Amazon SNS Extended Client Libraries publish messages larger than 256 KiB by storing the payload in Amazon S3, with a maximum payload size of 2 GB, so the choice is between a native 1 MiB message on a restricted topic and a pointer-based message of up to 2 GB on an unrestricted one.
svg.title: The attribute that quadruples the payload also removes the fan-out
svg.text: Not a bigger topic — a different one
MaximumMessageSize reads like a tuning knob. It changes what is allowed to subscribe.
Default standard topic
message size ≤ 262,144 bytes (256 KiB)
Fans out to everything SNS supports
SQS · Lambda · Firehose
HTTP/S · email · SMS · mobile push
Subscriptions quota:
12,500,000 per topic
(FIFO topics: 100 per topic)
MaximumMessageSize raised above 256 KiB
message size ≤ 1 MiB — a 4x increase
Supports three subscription types only
Amazon SQS · Amazon Data Firehose · AWS Lambda
No HTTP/S, email, SMS or mobile push.
Subscriptions ceiling:
100 per topic
Firehose binds earlier: 5 per topic, per subscription owner.
It is a trade, not an upgrade
The same attribute that quadruples the payload removes every human-facing protocol and collapses the
subscription ceiling. Most estates will want both shapes — on different topics.
And the older path still goes much further
The Extended Client Libraries store the payload in S3 and publish a reference — “the maximum payload size is 2 GB” — with fan-out intact.
Native 1 MiB is simpler with a hard wall. The library is more moving parts and two thousand times the headroom.
Inventory subscriptions by protocol before setting the attribute. Anything that is not SQS, Firehose or Lambda has to move or stay behind.
No pricing statement was made in the announcement — check the pricing page before modelling a migration at volume.
